title: The statements: the Riemann hypothesis and the generalised Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, in three forms
summary: Four propositions, stated with Mathlib's ζ and Dirichlet L-functions only (the module imports nothing but Mathlib): zeros of ζ off the trivial zeros and off s = 1 lie on Re s = 1/2; no Dirichlet L-function vanishes on Re s > 1/2 (the point s = 1 of a principal character excepted); zeros of Dirichlet L-functions in the open strip 0 < Re s < 1 lie on Re s = 1/2; the same for primitive characters. They are the types of the five theorems of `Main` (unit 155).

members.name: RiemannZetaZerosOnLine
members.text: The proposition RiemannZetaZerosOnLine (the Riemann hypothesis): for every complex number s, if ζ(s) = 0, if s is not of the form −2(n + 1) for any natural number n (that is, s is none of the trivial zeros −2, −4, −6, …), and if s ≠ 1, then Re s = 1/2. Here ζ is Mathlib's `riemannZeta`, the meromorphic continuation of ∑_{n≥1} n^{−s} to ℂ; Mathlib defines it at every complex number, also at the pole s = 1, where it takes a conventional finite value.

members.name: DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf
members.text: The proposition DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf (the generalised Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, in half-plane form): for every natural number N with N ≠ 0 (Lean's instance argument `NeZero N`), every Dirichlet character χ modulo N with complex values, and every complex number s with 1/2 < Re s, if χ is not the principal character modulo N or s ≠ 1, then L(s, χ) ≠ 0. Here L(s, χ) is Mathlib's `DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s`, the meromorphic continuation of ∑_{n≥1} χ(n) n^{−s} (for the principal character it has a pole at s = 1, where Mathlib assigns a conventional value); a Dirichlet character modulo N is Mathlib's `DirichletCharacter ℂ N`, a multiplicative map ℤ/N → ℂ that vanishes off the units, and `1` is the principal character modulo N (1 on the units, 0 elsewhere).

members.name: DirichletLZerosOnLine
members.text: The proposition DirichletLZerosOnLine (the generalised Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, critical-strip form): for every natural number N with N ≠ 0 (instance `NeZero N`), every Dirichlet character χ modulo N with complex values, and every complex number s with 0 < Re s and Re s < 1 and L(s, χ) = 0, one has Re s = 1/2. Here L(s, χ) is Mathlib's `DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s`, the meromorphic continuation of ∑_{n≥1} χ(n) n^{−s} (for the principal character it has a pole at s = 1, where Mathlib assigns a conventional value); a Dirichlet character modulo N is Mathlib's `DirichletCharacter ℂ N`, a multiplicative map ℤ/N → ℂ that vanishes off the units, and `1` is the principal character modulo N (1 on the units, 0 elsewhere).

members.name: PrimitiveDirichletLZerosOnLine
members.text: The proposition PrimitiveDirichletLZerosOnLine (the same for primitive characters only): for every natural number N with N ≠ 0 (instance `NeZero N`) and every Dirichlet character χ modulo N with complex values that is primitive (Mathlib's `DirichletCharacter.IsPrimitive`: the conductor of χ equals N), and for every complex number s with 0 < Re s and Re s < 1 and L(s, χ) = 0, one has Re s = 1/2. Here L(s, χ) is Mathlib's `DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s`, the meromorphic continuation of ∑_{n≥1} χ(n) n^{−s} (for the principal character it has a pole at s = 1, where Mathlib assigns a conventional value); a Dirichlet character modulo N is Mathlib's `DirichletCharacter ℂ N`, a multiplicative map ℤ/N → ℂ that vanishes off the units, and `1` is the principal character modulo N (1 on the units, 0 elsewhere).

ambient_inputs.name: riemannZeta
ambient_inputs.text: The Riemann zeta function ζ : ℂ → ℂ: for Re s > 1 the sum ∑_{n≥1} n^{−s}, continued meromorphically to ℂ with a simple pole at s = 1 (Mathlib defines it as the even Hurwitz zeta function at 0); as a Lean function it is defined at every point, also at s = 1.

ambient_inputs.name: DirichletCharacter
ambient_inputs.lean: abbrev DirichletCharacter (R : Type*) [CommMonoidWithZero R] (n : ℕ) := MulChar (ZMod n) R
ambient_inputs.text: A Dirichlet character modulo N with values in R: a multiplicative character of ℤ/N (a multiplicative map ℤ/N → R sending non-units to 0); `1` is the principal character. It is evaluated at integers and natural numbers through the reduction to ℤ/N.

ambient_inputs.name: DirichletCharacter.LFunction
ambient_inputs.lean: noncomputable def LFunction (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) (s : ℂ) : ℂ := ZMod.LFunction χ s
ambient_inputs.text: For N ≠ 0 and a Dirichlet character χ modulo N with complex values, s ↦ L(s, χ): for Re s > 1 the series ∑_{n≥1} χ(n)n^{−s}, and its meromorphic continuation elsewhere (entire unless χ is principal; then a simple pole at s = 1, where the Lean function takes a conventional value).

ambient_inputs.name: DirichletCharacter.IsPrimitive
ambient_inputs.lean: def IsPrimitive : Prop := conductor χ = n
ambient_inputs.text: χ modulo N is primitive when its conductor (the least modulus through which it factors) equals N.
